items.followUp: What is the purpose of the body section in an HTML webpage?

rubric.why: Identifies the tags that enclose the head section.
rubric.description: Names the opening and closing head tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the head tags.

rubric.why: Shows what the head section contains or how it is used.
rubric.description: States that the head contains page information such as the title, which is generally not displayed in the webpage body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct purpose or example of head content.

modelAnswer: The head section is written between the <head> and </head> tags in an HTML document.
It contains information about the webpage, such as its title and metadata, which is generally not displayed in the page body.

items.followUp: Write two characteristics of a weak password.

rubric.why: Length and a mix of character types make a password harder to guess.
rubric.description: Gives one valid characteristic of a strong password, such as sufficient length or a mix of character types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid characteristic.

rubric.why: Avoiding predictable information improves password security.
rubric.description: Gives another valid characteristic, such as avoiding personal details or choosing a password that is difficult to guess.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second valid characteristic.

modelAnswer: A good password should be long and difficult to guess.
It should use a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and should not contain easily guessed personal information.

items.followUp: Write four notes on Bus Topology.

rubric.why: A star topology connects devices through a central device, and data passes through it.
rubric.description: Describes the central connection used in a star topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the central hub or switch and its role.

rubric.why: These are valid features or limitations of star topology.
rubric.description: Gives a valid practical advantage or limitation of star topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct point about adding devices or the effects of a failure.

modelAnswer: In a star topology, every computer is connected to a central hub or switch.
Data sent between computers passes through this central device.
A computer can usually be added or removed without disrupting the other computers.
If the central device fails, the whole network may stop working; a failure in one computer's link usually affects only that computer.
